questions.question: Inside a `sequence { }` builder you can call `delay()` between `yield`s to space the values out, just like you can between `emit`s inside `flow { }`.
questions.explanation: `SequenceScope` is marked `@RestrictsSuspension`, so the block may only call its own suspend functions (`yield`, `yieldAll`), and `delay` is a compile error. A sequence is pulled synchronously through a plain `Iterator`, so it can't really wait. Use `flow { }` when producing values needs to suspend.

questions.question: Why doesn't this compile?
options: `state` is inferred as `MutableStateFlow<UiState.Loading>`, so `Ok` can't be assigned
A `data object` can't be the initial value of a `MutableStateFlow`
`state.value` can only be set from inside a coroutine, because the setter suspends
`MutableStateFlow` needs a `data class` type for equality checks, not a sealed interface
questions.explanation: Type inference picks the most specific type of the argument, so `T` becomes `UiState.Loading`. Since `MutableStateFlow` is invariant, you need `MutableStateFlow<UiState>(UiState.Loading)`. Setting `value` isn't a suspend call, so it works outside coroutines.

questions.question: This doesn't compile. Which single changes make it compile? Select all that apply.
questions.code:
inline fun CoroutineScope.safeLaunch(block: suspend () -> Unit) =
    launch { block() }
options: Change the type to `suspend CoroutineScope.() -> Unit`
questions.explanation: `safeLaunch` isn't a suspend function, so it can't take an inlined `suspend` lambda, and `block` is also called inside `launch`'s lambda, which isn't inlined, so a non-local `return` from it would be impossible. `crossinline`, `noinline` or dropping `inline` fixes both. Changing the receiver fixes neither, and passing `block` as a value still requires `noinline`.

questions.question: What happens when you compile this?
options: Compile error: `distinctUntilChanged` on a `StateFlow` is deprecated at ERROR level
It compiles and prints nothing, because `distinctUntilChanged` drops the first value
It compiles but throws `IllegalStateException` when the flow is first collected
questions.explanation: A `StateFlow` already skips values equal to the current one, so adding `distinctUntilChanged()` does nothing. kotlinx.coroutines marks that overload as deprecated at ERROR level to catch the mistake. Remove the call and the code prints `0`.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.code:
import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*

data class Cart(val items: MutableList<String>)

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val state = MutableStateFlow(Cart(mutableListOf("a")))
    val job = launch { state.collect { println(it.items) } }
    yield()
    val next = state.value.copy()
    next.items.add("b")
    state.value = next
    yield()
    job.cancel()
}
questions.explanation: `copy()` is shallow, so `next` shares the same `MutableList` as the current value. Adding `"b"` changes both. Now `next == state.value`, so the `StateFlow` treats the assignment as no change and emits nothing. Use immutable lists and `copy(items = items + "b")`.

questions.question: What happens when you compile this?

It prints nothing, because `return` exits the launched coroutine
It prints `loaded`, because `return` only skips the current `forEach` item
It returns from `load` before the coroutine starts
questions.explanation: A bare `return` targets the nearest enclosing `fun`, here `load`. `forEach` is inline, but `launch`'s lambda isn't, and you can't return from `load` inside a coroutine that runs later. Write `return@launch` to end the coroutine or `return@forEach` to skip an item.

questions.question: In each setup, child `a` throws and child `b` is still in a long `delay`. In which setups is `b` cancelled? Select all that apply.
options: With `scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob())`: `scope.launch { launch { a() }; launch { b() } }`
questions.explanation: A regular Job cancels all its children when one child fails. A supervisor only protects its direct children. In the nested `scope.launch { ... }` case, `a` and `b` are children of that outer `launch`, which has an ordinary Job, so `b` is cancelled. In the other supervisor setups, `a` and `b` are direct children, so `b` keeps running.

questions.question: `loadProfile(cached)` is called with a non-null `cached`. What happens?
options: It suspends forever: `coroutineScope` waits for the never-started `fresh` child
It returns `cached` right away, and `fresh` is cancelled automatically when the scope ends
It returns `cached`, and `fetchProfile()` keeps running in the background
It throws `IllegalStateException` because a lazy `Deferred` was never awaited
questions.explanation: A `LAZY` async is still a child of the scope. `coroutineScope` can only complete when all its children have finished, and nothing ever starts `fresh`. The call hangs, for example leaving a ViewModel's loading spinner up. Call `fresh.cancel()` before returning, or only create the `async` when it's needed.
